    Top-seeded UConn defeated #6 Notre Dame 70-52 in the 2026 Elite Eight, led by Sarah Strong’s 21 points and 8 rebounds, and Blanca Quiñonez’s 20 points off the bench. Hannah Hidalgo led Notre Dame with 22 points and 11 rebounds. UConn dominated after a 10-0 second-quarter run, securing a Final Four berth.

    How much is Geno Auriemma paid?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Geno Auriemma signed a five-year contract extension with UConn in June 2024, valued at $18.7 million, making him one of the highest-paid coaches in women's basketball. For the 2024-25 season, his pay is approximately $3.34 million, including a $400,000 base salary and $2.94 million in additional compensation, increasing annually through 2029. 
    Key Details of Auriemma's Contract (2024-2029): 
    • Total Value: $18.7 million over five years (through April 2029).
    • Annual Salary (2024-25): $3.34 million ($400,000 base + $2.94 million in media/speaking/consulting).
    • Salary Growth:
      Compensation increases by $200,000 each year.
    • Bonuses: The deal includes performance-based incentives.
    • Compensation Structure: Auriemma's contract includes substantial compensation for speaking, consulting, and media obligations. 
    Auriemma's contract also includes a significantly increased buyout clause, rising to $5 million if he leaves for another job in women's basketball, which drops by $500,000 each year.
